prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1169; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed first notice of loss. Insured reports vehicle was struck on the driver side while insured was turning left at an intersection. Police report requested. Insured states the other vehicle was approaching from the opposite direction. No statement taken yet from the other driver.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office. Claimant reports neck and back strain following the collision and is under treatment. Attorney requested that all further contact be routed through their office. Written confirmation of representation received and placed in file.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report. Responding officer noted both vehicles had damage consistent with a side impact at low to moderate speed. Citation issued to the other driver for failure to yield on a left turn. Scene photos reviewed and added to the file.

Entry 4: Received medical records from the claimant's attorney. Treating provider documents cervical and lumbar strain with muscle spasm and restricted range of motion. Follow-up visits scheduled. Medical file flagged for review by the bodily injury unit. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect the injury claim.

Entry 5: Liability position reviewed. Based on the police report and the other driver's citation, liability appears to rest primarily with the other party. Recommend proceeding with a demand evaluation once treatment is complete and the attorney submits a formal demand package. Diary set for follow-up in thirty days.
